**Surah al-Taghabun**

It is Meccan (*Makkiyyah*) according to what appears from its counterparts for one who examines them. It is also said to be Madinan (*Madaniyyah*). Its verses number eighteen.

**Commentary on His saying, exalted is He:**

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah. To Him belongs dominion, and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent.﴾ ﴿He is the one who created you, so among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ [At-Taghabun: 2]

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah. To Him belongs dominion﴾, i.e., the dominion of the heavens and the earth and the execution of command within them. ﴿And to Him belongs praise﴾, i.e., fine commendation, because He is the source of blessings and the One who brings them into existence.

﴿Has there not come to you the news of those who disbelieved before? So they tasted the evil of their affair, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ [At-Taghabun: 5] ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, and they said, "Shall mere humans guide us?" So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was self-sufficient, and Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy.﴾ [At-Taghabun: 6]

I.e., He is the One who alone originated you in the best of forms, capable of perfections both in knowledge and in action. Yet among you is one who chooses disbelief, denies the truth, and earns it contrary to what his nature calls for; and among you is one who chooses faith and earns it in accordance with what his nature requires. It was obligatory upon you all to choose faith and to be thankful for the blessing of creation and origination, and for what branches from it of all other blessings. But you did not do that, although you had full capacity for it; rather, you split into branches and divided into sects. The mention of disbelief first is because it is the predominant trait among them, and it is more fitting to the context of rebuke, as Abu al-Su'ud (*Abu al-Su'ud*) stated.

﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾ [At-Taghabun: 2], i.e., He will recompense you for it. So prefer what benefits you, and keep away from what ruins you.

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[3] ﴿He created the heavens and the earth with truth, and formed you and perfected your forms, and to Him is the final return.﴾

﴿He created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾ — that is, with far-reaching wisdom, which guides to the religious and worldly benefits. ﴿And formed you and perfected your forms﴾ — that is, He brought you into being in the best of proportion. This is because He, exalted is He, made man upright in stature, with the most balanced temperaments, and gave him intellect (ʿaql), the power of speech, the capacity to act upon created things, and the ability to practise all kinds of crafts. ﴿And to Him is the final return﴾ — that is, your return for recompense.

﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you disclose, and Allah is Knowing of the contents of the breasts.﴾ That is, of their hidden matters and what they harbor within themselves. It affirms what precedes it and serves as evidence for it, for when He knows the secrets and the hidden thoughts of hearts, nothing hidden among all created beings is concealed from Him.

Al-Zamakhshari said: By His knowledge of what is in the heavens and the earth, He drew attention, then by His knowledge of what the servants conceal and disclose, then by His knowledge of the contents of the breasts, that nothing of the universals and particulars is hidden from Him or absent from Him. Therefore He is the one who must be feared and guarded against, and no one should dare to do anything that opposes His pleasure. The repetition of knowledge has the sense of repeating the warning. Everything He mentioned after His saying, ﴿So among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [At-Taghabun: 2], as you see, carries the sense of a warning against disbelief, and a denunciation of disobeying the Creator and failing to thank His blessing. End of quotation.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[5–6] ﴿Has there not come to you the news of those who disbelieved before? So they tasted the bad outcome of their affair, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, and they said, "Shall mere humans guide us?" So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was free of need. And Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy.﴾ [at-Taghabun: 6]

﴿Has there not come to you﴾, i.e., O assembly of disbelievers and wicked ones, ﴿a painful punishment﴾. ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, and they said, "Shall mere humans guide us?"﴾ [at-Taghabun: 6], i.e., like the people of Noah, ʿAd, Thamud, and the people of Lot. ﴿So they tasted the bad outcome of their affair﴾ from the punishment of annihilation. Al-wabal (the bad outcome) is the heaviness and the severity that follows from a matter of affairs. And ﴿their affair﴾ is their disbelief; He expressed it thus to signal that it is a monstrous matter and a great crime. ﴿And for them﴾, i.e., in the Hereafter, ﴿is a painful punishment﴾. ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, and they said, "Shall mere humans guide us?"﴾ [at-Taghabun: 6], i.e., that mentioned tasting of the bad outcome of their affair in this world, and what has been prepared for them of the punishment of the Hereafter, is because their messengers came to them with the clear evidences and signs regarding the truth of what they called them to. So they rejected them, followed their desires, mocked their messengers, and said: "Shall mere humans guide us?"

Ibn Jarir said: out of arrogance on their part, that Allah's messengers to them should be humans like themselves, and arrogance against following the truth because a human like them called them to it.

The report about "humans" was given in the plural, so it says ﴿yahduunana﴾ [at-Taghabun: 6] and not "yahdina," because "basharun" (human), though singular in form, carries the meaning of a plural. End of quote.

Al-Qashani said: When they were veiled by the attributes of their souls from the Light by which He surpasses them beyond comparison, and they found from Him nothing but humanity, they denied His guidance. For every knower is known only through the meaning that is in him, so the perfect light is found only through the innate light, and only the perfect know perfection. For this reason it has been said: "None knows Allah except Allah." Every seeker who has found his sought-after in some aspect is directed toward what makes turning toward it possible; likewise every one who affirms something possesses the meaning he affirms, through that meaning within himself. Since there was none of the innate light in them at all, they did not recognize perfection from Him, so they denied it, and they recognized none of the truth, so no seeking arose in them that would require them to need guidance; thus they denied guidance.

﴿So they disbelieved﴾ [at-Taghabun: 6], i.e., in the truth, the religion, and the Messenger. ﴿And turned away﴾ [at-Taghabun: 6], i.e., from reflecting upon the clear signs. ﴿And Allah was free of need﴾ [at-Taghabun: 6], i.e., He manifested His independence from their faith and obedience, in that He destroyed them and cut off their last trace; had He not been free of need from them, He would not have done that. So "istaghna" (was free of need) is conjoined to what precedes it, and it is permitted to make it a circumstantial clause with "qad" implied, i.e., "and He had become free of need through His perfection, whether they knew it or not."

﴿And Allah is Free of need﴾ [at-Taghabun: 6], i.e., in His essence from the worlds, let alone their faith; no perfection of His perfections depends upon them, nor upon their knowledge of Him.

﴿Praiseworthy﴾ [at-Taghabun: 6], i.e., every creature praises Him, or He is deserving of praise in Himself, even if no one who praises Him exists.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[7] ﴿The disbelievers claim that they will never be resurrected. Say: "Yes, by my Lord, you will certainly be resurrected, then you will certainly be informed of what you did. That is easy for Allah."﴾

﴿The disbelievers claim that they will never be resurrected. Say: "Yes, by my Lord, you will certainly be resurrected"﴾, i.e., from your graves. ﴿Then you will certainly be informed of what you did﴾, i.e., in the world. ﴿That is easy for Allah﴾, i.e., it is effortless for Him to bring the substance into being and for His complete power to be established.

Ibn Kathir said: This is the third verse in which Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to swear by his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, concerning the occurrence and existence of the Return (ma'ad). The first is in Yunus: ﴿And they ask you, "Is it true?" Say: "Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true."﴾ [Yunus: 53]. The second is in Saba': ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say: "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you."﴾ [Saba': 3]. The third is this verse.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 64, verse 8:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[8] ﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger, and in the light which We have sent down. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾ That is: since the matter is as such, then believe in Allah alone and in His Messenger regarding what he informs you of concerning the Resurrection (al-ba'th), the recompense (al-jaza'), and other things. ﴿And the light which We have sent down﴾ means the Wise Qur'an. The shift to the first-person plural "We" (nun al-'azama, the plural of majesty) serves to manifest the utmost care regarding the matter of the sending down. ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[9] ﴿The Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering, that is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain. And whoever believes in God and does righteous deeds, He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.﴾

﴿The Day He gathers you﴾ is an adverbial of time (ẓarf) governed either by ﴿you will be informed﴾ or by ﴿Aware﴾, because of the sense of warning (waʿīd) it contains. It is as if it were said: "And God will recompense you on the Day He gathers you." Or it is an object governed by ﴿remember﴾, meaning: "For the Day on which the first and the last will be gathered," that is, for the sake of the reckoning and recompense that take place on it. ﴿That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain.﴾ Al-Zamakhshari said: "Taghābun (mutual loss and gain) is used metaphorically from the expression taghābana al-qawm fī al-tijāra (the people cheated one another in trade), which means that some of them deceive others, because the happy will descend to the places of the wretched that they would have occupied had they been wretched, and the wretched will descend to the places of the happy that they would have occupied had they been happy. In this there is also a mockery of the wretched, since their descent is not a loss." End of quotation.

Among the things that make the use of taghābun for what has been mentioned appropriate is the occurrence of the language of selling and buying with regard to both groups. God mentions regarding the disbelievers that they bought the worldly life in exchange for the Hereafter and bought error in exchange for guidance, and He states that their commerce did not profit them. Thus it is as if they cheated themselves. And He directed the believers to a profitable commerce, saying: ﴿Shall I direct you to a commerce that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 10], and so on. He also states that they sold themselves for Paradise, so the deal of the disbelievers was a loss, and the deal of the believers was a gain.

Al-Qashani said: That is, the mutual loss and gain does not concern worldly matters, for they are transient things, swiftly passing away, necessarily perishing, none of which remains for anyone. If something of these is lost, or someone causes it to be lost, even if it be his life, then what has been lost or caused to be lost is only that whose loss was necessary; so there is truly no loss and no injustice. Rather, loss and mutual loss lie in the forfeiture of something which, had it not been forfeited, would have remained forever, and its possessor would have benefited from it eternally, namely the perfect and potential light. There, regret and mutual loss will appear in the squandering of profit and capital in the commerce of success and salvation, as He said: ﴿So their commerce did not profit them, nor were they guided﴾ [al-Baqara: 16]. Whoever squanders his potential and the light of his primordial nature is utterly defrauded, like one whose light has been taken and who remains in darkness. And whoever retains the light of his primordial nature but does not acquire the perfection befitting it, which his potential requires, or acquires some of it but does not reach its goal, is defrauded in comparison with the complete and perfect one. It is as if the complete one has attained his station and aim, while this one remains bewildered in his deficiency. End of quotation.

﴿And whoever believes in God and does righteous deeds, He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.﴾

(p-5823)

The commentary on His saying (Exalted is He):

[12–13] ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon Our Messenger is only the clear delivery (of the message).﴾ ﴿Allah – there is no deity except Him. And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾ [At-Taghabun: 13]

﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon Our Messenger is only the clear delivery (of the message).﴾ That is, (the delivery) of that with which he was sent. And Allah, glorified is He, is the Possessor of retribution against whoever disobeys Him and opposes His command.

﴿Allah – there is no deity except Him. And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾ [At-Taghabun: 13] Ibn Kathir said: The first (clause) is a report about al-tawhid (the affirmation of Allah's oneness), and its meaning is a command, i.e., affirm the divinity as belonging to Him alone, make it sincere for Him, and rely upon Him, as He said: ﴿Lord of the East and the West; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as a trustee (wakīl).﴾ [Al-Muzzammil: 9]

**The discourse on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying:**

[14] ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon and overlook and forgive, then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them﴾ This is an address to those who believed in the Prophet (ﷺ). Some of their wives and children opposed them because of their faith and harmed them on its account, and this distressed them and sometimes drove them to lash out at them. So they were commanded to beware of their trial (fitnah) and their polytheism (shirk) alone, and to conduct themselves toward them in the manner of people of virtue, as He said: ﴿And that you pardon﴾ [al-Baqarah: 237], meaning: for their sins. ﴿And overlook﴾, meaning: by refraining from reproach and rebuke. ﴿And forgive﴾, meaning: their offenses, with mercy toward them. ﴿Then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: He will treat you in the same manner as you have acted.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, who said: A man would embrace Islam, and his family and sons would blame him, so this verse was revealed.

And from Ibn Abbas, who said: When a man intended to emigrate from Makkah to Madinah, his wife and child would prevent him, and they would not cease discouraging him from that. So Allah said: "Indeed, they are an enemy to you, so beware of them, and listen and obey, and proceed to your affair." Afterward, whenever a man was prevented and discouraged, he would pass by his family and swear that he would surely do it and would surely punish his family for that. So Allah, Exalted is His praise, said: ﴿But if you pardon and overlook﴾, the verse...

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[15] ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial, and with Allah is a great reward.﴾

﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾ [al-Anfal: 28], meaning: the soul is tempted by them, and trials come upon it through them when they are preferred over the love of the Truth.

﴿And with Allah is a great reward﴾, meaning: for the one who prefers obedience to Allah and love of Him over them.

Ibn Jarir narrated from al-Dahhak, who said: This concerns people from the tribes of the Arabs. A man or a group from the clan would embrace Islam, and they would leave their clans, leaving their wives, children and fathers, intending to go to the Prophet (ﷺ). Then their clans, wives, children and fathers would stand up, appealing to them by Allah (p-5826) not to leave them and not to prefer anyone else over them. Some of them would soften and return to them, and others would proceed until they joined the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ).

And from Mujahid: A man carries his wealth and his child toward severing the ties of kinship, or toward disobedience to his Lord, so a man, with his love for them, cannot but obey them in this. Therefore, for preferring the obedience of Allah and fulfilling the right of Allah in wealth, he is promised a great reward, which is Paradise.

[16] The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able, and listen, and obey, and spend; it is better for yourselves. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul, those are the successful.﴾

﴿Fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ means: with your utmost effort and capacity. That is, exert your ability in it. ﴿And listen and obey﴾ means: understand these commands and act upon them. ﴿And spend﴾ means: your wealth, which Allah has tested you with, in what pleases Him. ﴿It is better for yourselves﴾ means: and bring about good for yourselves, that is, aim in regard to wealth and children at what is best for you. Here, "khayran" (good) is the object (maf'ul bihi) of an implied verb. This is the view of Sibawayh, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Desist; it is better for you﴾ (An-Nisa: 171). It has also been said that its implied sense is: "Let spending be good," so it is the predicate of an implied "yakun" (be). This is the view of Abu 'Ubayd. It has also been said that it is the object of "anfiqu" (spend). This is the opinion of Ibn Jarir, who said: That is, "and spend some of your wealth for your own selves, so that you may rescue yourselves from the punishment of Allah, and the good in this context is wealth." ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul﴾ means: by being preserved from it. ﴿Those are the successful﴾ means: the attainers, who have achieved their aims with their Lord.

(p-5827)

The Explanation of His Words, exalted is He:

[17–18] ﴿If you lend to Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allah is Most Appreciative, Forbearing.﴾ ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ [at-Taghabun: 18]

﴿If you lend to Allah a goodly loan﴾ means: by spending in His cause from what you love, without reminder or harm. Al-Zamakhshari said: mentioning the loan is a gentle way of soliciting (spending). ﴿He will multiply it for you﴾ means: He will multiply its reward and its replacement. ﴿And forgive you﴾ means: your sins, by overlooking them. ﴿And Allah is Most Appreciative﴾ means: He is One who gives thanks to those who spend in His cause, by granting them a good reward for what they spent. ﴿Forbearing﴾ means: toward those who disobey Him, by not hastening to punish them.

﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾ [at-Taghabun: 18] means: what is hidden from the eyes of His servants and what they witness. ﴿The Almighty﴾ [at-Taghabun: 18] means: the Overpowering in His retribution against those who oppose His command and prohibition. ﴿The All-Wise﴾ [at-Taghabun: 18] means: in His management of His creation and His turning of them toward what benefits them.
